evidence_items.publisher: Dodge et al.; EMNLP 2021, arXiv version
evidence_items.locator: Section 5.3, paragraph reporting dialect exclusion rates
evidence_items.explanation: The audit reports removal rates of 42% for African American English and 32% for Hispanic-aligned English, against 6.2% for White-aligned English. This documents unequal exclusion from a web-scraped training corpus, using dialect as a proxy rather than identifying authors.

The audit documents sexualized retrieval for ordinary feminine and demographic terms, including terms referring to minority women. This supports unequal representational harm, although the exploratory searches do not estimate its population-wide prevalence.

evidence_items.locator: Section 7, Broader Impacts, FairFace bias probes and Table 6
evidence_items.explanation: CLIP's audit reports nonhuman classifications for approximately 14% of Black images, versus under 8% for every other racial group. It also qualifies any universal gender claim: crime-related misclassification affected male images more often than female images, 16.5% versus 9.8%.

unresolved_gaps: These studies do not provide a representative estimate of the distribution of all downstream AI harms.
